definition: The Nortel Speech Server (formerly known as Periphonics Speech Processing Platform) in telecommunications is a speech processing system that was originally developed by Nortel.
details: Following the bankruptcy of Nortel, it is now sold by Avaya. The system is primarily used for large vocabulary speech recognition, natural language understanding, text-to-speech, and speaker verification. The Nortel Speech Server was based on the Periphonics OSCAR platform. The original OSCAR Platform was based upon Solaris servers. The current range of Speech Servers is Windows based. Nortel Speech Server is a component of the MPS 500, MPS 1000, and ICP platforms. On MPS systems, it may be used to stream prerecorded audio.

explainer.lead: Nortel Speech Server is a telecommunications speech processing system originally developed by Nortel, formerly the Periphonics Speech Processing Platform. It matters because it provides large vocabulary speech recognition, natural language understanding, text-to-speech, and speaker verification in telephony platforms.

tiers.eli5: It is the phone system's built-in listener and talker, understanding spoken words and speaking back to callers.
tiers.practitioner: It is deployed as a component of the MPS 500, MPS 1000, and ICP platforms. A consideration is platform lineage: the original OSCAR platform ran on Solaris servers, while the current range of Speech Servers is Windows based.
tiers.paperLevel: A speech processing system based on the Periphonics OSCAR platform, used primarily for large vocabulary speech recognition, natural language understanding, text-to-speech, and speaker verification. After Nortel's bankruptcy it is sold by Avaya.

explainer.example: On an MPS system, the Speech Server handles a caller's spoken input and generates spoken responses within the telephony platform.
